items: **d-ary**: fewer levels (log_d n) but d child compares per level — wins when decreases dominate comparisons (cache lines hold d children)
**deadline scheduling**: sort by deadline asc; keep duration max-heap; if time exceeds deadline, evict longest task (maximize tasks kept)
**external top-k**: chunk to disk sorted desc, frontier heap over chunk heads — memory bounded by k + buffers
**Huffman**: min-PQ merge two least, push combined; Σ depth×freq optimal prefix code

chain.a: Lazy melding O(1) amortized join, good constants in practice despite weak worst-case bounds; pb_ds pairing_heap_tag exposes modify()=decrease-key.
Two-heaps still correct; memory forces count-based structures or quantile sketches (t-digest class) — mention approximation tier.

chain.q: Heap vs sorted-vector for fixed dataset many queries?
chain.a: Sorted vector wins: build once Θ(n log n), binary searches O(log n), better cache; heaps shine under interleaved inserts.
Heap ops iterative — no recursion depth issues; contrast recursive DFS solutions needing explicit stacks.
